roadmap_note_operation_identity_vs_share.principle: This review demonstrates a discovery-architecture gap worth fixing structurally: 'shares a funder/provisioner' and 'is the same operation' are currently conflated by construction in every family-building step that uses HAVING COUNT(*)>=N on a single funder column. A private root funding 23 otherwise-unconnected wallets with zero independent internal corroboration (dimension 10 of this review) produces the exact same STRONG_CANDIDATE_FAMILY signature as a genuinely unified single-operator operation would. Future discovery architecture should carry an explicit, first-class 'internal corroboration strength' field alongside family/member counts -- distinguishing FUNDER-COHERENT (one shared source, no other links) from OPERATION-COHERENT (shared source PLUS independent secondary evidence, e.g. non-Dv34-routed secondary funders, shared post-migration behavior, or shared timing clusters not explainable by the funder alone) -- so that 'private provisioning network' and 'operation' are never silently treated as synonyms downstream.
roadmap_note_operation_identity_vs_share.concrete_next_step: add an internal_corroboration_strength field (computed the way compute_internal_subfamilies()/compute_dv34_internal_boundary_counterfactual() do here) to candidate_families at construction time in the local_operation_discovery pipeline, not just as a bolt-on post-hoc review.

next_human_decision: Human reviewer decides among the disposition_options above; this review does not force a single answer. No canonical mutation, no Watchtower promotion, and no operation membership creation has occurred as part of producing this artifact.
terminal_verdict: DV34_OPERATION_IDENTITY_PARTIALLY_RESOLVED -- separateness from CONFIRMED Watchtower is independently supported (dimension 9, NO); internal operational unity of the 23-member family (single operation vs. provisioning network) is NOT independently resolved (dimension 10, 0/23 clustered) and remains a candidate-tier open question
